composition.story: A Llama decoder block receives one vector per token. Attention and the MLP each read a normalized copy of that stream, then add their result back. Step through to see the stream keep its shape while gaining two additions.

aha.observation: The block never replaces the stream: its output is the input plus an attention update plus an MLP update, so the shape stays the same.

controls.label: Step
controls.presentation: Previous and Next buttons; keyboard arrows; names kept when disabled at ends

states.label: Stream enters
states.sentence: Each token arrives as one vector; together they form the residual stream that runs through the block.
states.why: This stream is what the block will update.

states.label: Normalize copy
states.sentence: RMSNorm rescales a copy of every token vector. The original stream waits on the skip path, untouched.
states.why: Attention should read scaled values, not the raw stream.

states.label: Attention mixes tokens
states.sentence: Attention applies RoPE to queries and keys, then each token blends values from itself and earlier tokens.
states.why: This is the only place tokens exchange information.

states.label: Add attention update
states.sentence: The attention result is added to the original stream, not substituted for it.
states.why: The skip path keeps the earlier information intact.

states.label: Normalize again
states.sentence: A second RMSNorm rescales a copy of the updated stream for the feed-forward part.
states.why: The MLP also reads a normalized copy.

states.label: MLP transforms each token
states.sentence: SwiGLU gates one projection with another, then projects back down. Each token is processed separately.
states.why: This step transforms tokens independently, without mixing them.

states.label: Add MLP update
states.sentence: The MLP result is added to the stream. Output equals input plus attention update plus MLP update.
states.why: Shape is unchanged, so identical blocks can be stacked.
